own_solution.law: Series capacitance C = C1 C2/(C1 + C2); stored energy U = (1/2) C V^2 at full charge
assumptions: fully charged, i.e. steady state reached

T12E2.regime: voltage across the 4 μF capacitor (75 V) below its 185 V rating, so no breakdown

T4707.regime: voltage across the 4 μF capacitor (75 V) below its 185 V limit

TE79C.regime: full charge, t >> RC (stated 'fully charged'); R affects only the charging transient

TCCF3.regime: full charge, t >> RC; R affects only the transient

defect_reasons.other: With a 7.5 μF capacitor added in parallel with the second (TF8B9, TFF02), 'energy stored in the two capacitors together' can mean the 4 μF and 12 μF only (0.01551 J) or the whole network including the added one (0.01660 J).

notes: Base: C = 3 μF, Q = 300 μC, V1 = 75 V, V2 = 25 V, U = 0.5*3e-6*100^2 = 0.015 J. With 7.5 μF parallel to 12 μF: C2' = 19.5 μF, Ceq = 78/23.5 = 3.3191 μF, Q = 331.91 μC, V1 = 82.98 V, V2 = 17.02 V. Energy in 4 μF = 0.013771 J, in 12 μF = 0.001738 J, sum 0.01551 J; including the 7.5 μF (0.001086 J) total = 0.01660 J. I report the literal reading (the two named capacitors). Resistance sentences: R does not affect final stored energy given 'fully charged'; I classed them K (regime t >> RC), though C is defensible. There is a mild tension between 'the connecting wires have negligible resistance' and 'the charging circuit offers a resistance of 6.5 kΩ', not a contradiction since the resistance could be elsewhere. The voltage-rating sentences are K since 75 V < 185 V. The problem text has a comma splice ('start uncharged, the connecting wires...').
